{{Short description|Biologist (born 1962)}}
[[File:Neutrophil_Extracellular_Trap.jpg|thumb|300x300px|Arturo Zychlinsky discovered [[Neutrophil extracellular traps|Neutrophil Extracellular Traps]] (NETs) together with Volker Brinkmann. This scanning electron image shows a NET (green), ejected by a neutrophil (yellow) to capture bacteria (purple). A red blood cell (orange) is also trapped in the NET. ]]
'''Arturo Zychlinsky''' (born 1962) is a biologist and since 2001 director at the [[Max Planck Institute for Infection Biology]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Organization chart|url=https://www.mpiib-berlin.mpg.de/institute/organization/chart|access-date=2021-05-07|website=www.mpiib-berlin.mpg.de|language=en}}</ref> His research focuses on [[Neutrophil extracellular traps|Neutrophil Extracellular Traps]] (NETs) which he discovered together with [[Volker Brinkmann]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Brinkmann|first1=Volker|last2=Reichard|first2=Ulrike|last3=Goosmann|first3=Christian|last4=Fauler|first4=Beatrix|last5=Uhlemann|first5=Yvonne|last6=Weiss|first6=David S.|last7=Weinrauch|first7=Yvette|last8=Zychlinsky|first8=Arturo|date=2004-03-05|title=Neutrophil extracellular traps kill bacteria|journal=Science|volume=303|issue=5663|pages=1532–1535|doi=10.1126/science.1092385|issn=1095-9203|pmid=15001782|bibcode=2004Sci...303.1532B |s2cid=21628300 }}</ref> and the immune function of [[chromatin]].

== Life ==
Arturo Zychlinsky completed his undergraduate studies at the Escuela Nacional de Ciencias Biológicas in [[Mexico City]]. In 1991, he obtained his PhD at the [[Rockefeller University]] where he trained with Ding-E Young in the laboratory of [[Zanvil A. Cohn|Zanvil Cohn]]. From 1991 to 1993 he was an EMBO postdoctoral fellow with [[Philippe Sansonetti|Philippe J. Sansonetti]] at the Institut Pasteur. He then moved to the Skirball Institute, [[New York University Grossman School of Medicine|New York University School of Medicine]], where he took a position as Assistant and Associate Professor. Since 2001, he is director of the Department for Cellular Microbiology at the Max Planck Institute for Infection Biology in Berlin.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Cellular Microbiology|url=https://www.mpiib-berlin.mpg.de/research/cellular_microbiology|access-date=2021-05-06|website=www.mpiib-berlin.mpg.de|language=en}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Arturo Zychlinsky received the Irma T. Hirschl Career Scientist Award, and the Eva and Klaus Grohe Award of the Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences.<ref>{{Cite web|title=2005 – Berlin-Brandenburgische Akademie der Wissenschaften|url=https://www.bbaw.de/die-akademie/auszeichnungen/preise/eva-und-klaus-grohe-preis-der-akademie/2005|access-date=2021-05-06|website=www.bbaw.de|archive-date=2021-05-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210506205715/https://www.bbaw.de/die-akademie/auszeichnungen/preise/eva-und-klaus-grohe-preis-der-akademie/2005}}</ref> He is a member of the [[European Molecular Biology Organization]] (EMBO), the [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mitglieder|url=https://www.leopoldina.org/mitgliederverzeichnis/mitglieder/member/Member/show/arturo-zychlinsky/|access-date=2021-05-06|website=Nationale Akademie der Wissenschaften Leopoldina|language=de}}</ref> the American Society and Academy of Microbiology, and the [[European Academy of Microbiology]].

== Personal life ==
Zychlinsky is married to the German zoologist and neuroethologist [[Constance Scharff]]; they have two daughters.{{citation needed|date=May 2021}}
